title: Persist the review flow: finding lineage, invalidation and carry-forward
description:
Objective: compose @moe/review's pure helpers into authenticated durable daemon services so J4 (rejection and re-plan) is drivable end to end. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09 from the Foundation canary's block report, verified on disk. One of the two remaining M1 exit blockers; the other is J3 (launcher/restart composition).

THE GAP, MEASURED 2026-08-09. `@moe/review` publishes a complete PURE surface from its package root - 23 symbols including recordReviewRound, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, assessReviewerIndependence, buildReviewPackage, findingFingerprint, reviewerCalibrationDigest, plus the frozen vocabularies REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS, REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS, REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE, REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS and REVIEW_PACKAGE_FORBIDDEN_ITEM_KINDS. Every rule J4 needs already exists and is reachable.

`apps/daemon/src` has NO review directory at all - only bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery and work. So there is no durable persistence for finding lineage, no changed-hash invalidation or carry-forward classification, no successor replan record, and no retained review records. The pure layer decides; nothing writes it down.

WHAT J4 REQUIRES, from design line 1101, transcribe it rather than trusting this summary: findings link evidence to required changes; delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated versus carry-forward nodes; the three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit; and old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan. That last clause is the immutability half and is the one most easily lost - a re-plan that rewrites history rather than appending a successor fails J4 even if every other assertion passes.

THIS IS COMPOSITION, NOT NEW DOMAIN LOGIC, which is what bounds it. The daemon service decodes, hands the parsed command to @moe/review's helpers, and commits their verdict durably through @moe/store's expected-version decision seam - the same shape bootstrap-services.ts:48 states as the house rule: "reduce, then commit only on acceptance". A handler that re-implements a rule @moe/review owns creates a second source of truth that will drift.

NOT in scope: new rules in @moe/review (its pure surface is complete and is consumed, not forked); J1's command path (task-671578e5); J3 launcher/restart composition; the E2E canary journeys themselves; any HTTP or transport change.

Hard dependencies: none - @moe/review and @moe/store are committed at HEAD and @moe/store is already an apps/daemon dependency.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/review/** and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts (command-kind vocabulary only).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: Review rounds are durably recorded through @moe/review's recordReviewRound and committed via the store's expected-version decision seam, so a round survives a restart and a replayed round returns the same terminal decision while leaving exactly one durable row — asserted by reading the row count back, not by the second call not throwing.

Finding lineage is append-only and readable after a re-plan: an earlier round's findings remain retrievable and byte-identical once a successor round exists. A re-plan that rewrites or drops prior findings fails this DoD even if every other assertion passes — design line 1101 requires old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews to remain readable.

Delta approval classifies every affected node as either INVALIDATED or CARRY_FORWARD by changed hash, with no third silent outcome and no node left unclassified. Assert the classification set by set equality against a hand-written list and assert the case count is non-zero, so a sweep that classifies nothing cannot pass.

The three-round counter is durable and escalation is explicit, tested AT the boundary: two unsuccessful rounds do not escalate, the third requires explicit escalation, and a fourth cannot proceed as if unescalated. The limit is read from @moe/review's REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT rather than a local constant.

Every refusal surfaces @moe/review's own reason code from REVIEW_REASON_CODES and names the refusing layer, never a locally invented code — asserted by feeding a case the pure layer rejects and pinning that exact code, so which layer refused survives the composition.

A finding that cannot satisfy independence or whose proof state is failed or unknown cannot produce an acceptance, and the attempt commits NOTHING — proven by reading the store back rather than by the returned value, since a service that mutates then refuses would pass a return-value-only assertion.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, and only owned paths are staged and committed by explicit pathspec.
taskRails: Compose, never decide. Every review rule lives in @moe/review already and is reachable from its package root. A daemon handler that restates one creates a second source of truth that will drift; if a needed rule seems missing, report_blocked rather than writing it here.

Import @moe/review from its package ROOT specifier only — never a deep subpath. The exports map is exclusive and deep imports do not resolve at runtime; this repo has lost several task-days to exactly that wall.

History is append-only. A re-plan appends a successor round and never rewrites, deletes or reclassifies an earlier one. Prove old records are still byte-identical after a successor exists, not merely that a new record was created.

Assert the reason code AND the refusing layer. Both the daemon's shape gate and a @moe/review validator can refuse the same input; a test asserting only 'refused' stays green if the shape gate starts answering first.
Prove non-mutation by reading the store back, never by trusting a returned value.
Read limits and vocabularies from @moe/review's exported constants — REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES — never a local copy, or the two drift silently.

Extend BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS by APPENDING only; existing suites assert against that array. Any new module needs its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — apps/daemon is now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate.

Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only; sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ in the same tree.

implementationPlan.description: Transcribe J4 from the design and pin the pure surface. Read design line 1101 directly (read-only — epic rail 1 forbids editing it) and write its four requirements into the step note by hand rather than trusting this task's paraphrase: findings link evidence to required changes; delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated versus carry-forward nodes; the three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit; and old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan. Then confirm on disk the 23 symbols @moe/review publishes from its ROOT — in particular recordReviewRound, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, assessReviewerIndependence, findingFingerprint, and the constants REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE. Confirm `apps/daemon/src/review/` does not exist. Read `bootstrap-services.ts:48` for the house handler shape and copy it rather than inventing a second idiom. Write down which pure helper answers each of the four J4 requirements — that mapping is the design of this task. If any requirement has no helper, report_blocked rather than planning to write the rule in the daemon. Produce no code.
implementationPlan.note:
J4 TRANSCRIBED BY HAND from the pinned design, line 1101 (read-only, not edited):

"**J4 - rejection and re-plan.** Findings link evidence to required changes. Delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated/carry-forward nodes. Three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit. Old plans, attempts, receipts, and reviews remain readable."

Four requirements, and the mapping to a pure helper for each — this mapping IS the design of the task:

1. FINDINGS LINK EVIDENCE TO REQUIRED CHANGES -> @moe/review `buildReviewPackage` binds the evidence (criteria / hashes / receipts / rubric / submittedBytes / tree) into one `reviewInputDigest`; `ReviewFinding.subject` ({kind: ARTIFACT|CRITERION|NODE|RECEIPT, locator}) is the typed required-change target and `findingFingerprint` is its identity (subject + ruleId only — detail and severity are deliberately unhashed). Daemon composes: a round is submitted against a built package and each finding names a bound locator.
2. DELTA APPROVAL SHOWS CHANGED HASHES AND INVALIDATED/CARRY-FORWARD NODES -> @moe/core `evaluateCarryForward` (packages/core/src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts:173), design 265's six conditions, `CARRY_FORWARD_HASH_MISMATCH` when sourceHash !== targetHash. Its module header states the division explicitly: "Core VALIDATES AND APPLIES a supplied impact set; it never computes one. Design 265 makes the graph diff the daemon's job" — so iterating the affected nodes is the daemon's job and the per-node verdict is the pure layer's. `valid:true` -> CARRY_FORWARD, `valid:false` -> INVALIDATED. `applyApprovalInvalidation` is the sibling for approval validity.
3. THREE-ROUND COUNTER VISIBLE, ESCALATION EXPLICIT -> `recordReviewRound` returns `lineage.unsuccessfulRounds` and routes ESCALATE with `REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED` at `REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT` (=3, read from the package, never copied); `qualifyReviewAcceptance` independently refuses at the cap so escalation cannot be skipped by going straight to acceptance.
4. OLD PLANS/ATTEMPTS/RECEIPTS/REVIEWS REMAIN READABLE -> `recordReviewRound` is append-only by construction: `round.round <= lastRound(lineage)` refuses `FINDING_LINEAGE_APPEND_ONLY`, and `lineageAttested` refuses `FINDING_LINEAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH` on a hand-reset counter or truncated records. Daemon composes by appending a new durable decision per round and never rewriting an earlier one.
5. (DoD 6, acceptance gate) -> `qualifyReviewAcceptance`: ELIGIBILITY (author / mutating lease / UNKNOWN independence / calibration) -> FINDINGS (round cap) -> ACCEPTANCE proof (PROOF_FAILED and PROOF_UNKNOWN are SEPARATE codes) -> ACCEPTANCE policy (@moe/core evaluatePolicy, codes carried verbatim).

Nothing is missing from the pure layer, so no report_blocked on rule ownership. All 23 @moe/review root exports confirmed on disk at packages/review/src/index.ts; `apps/daemon/src/review/` confirmed ABSENT (bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery, work only). House shape read at bootstrap-services.ts:48 ("reduce, then commit only on acceptance") and bootstrap-ledger.ts's two fail-open guards read in full.

DEVIATION, DECLARED NOT TAKEN — THE COMMAND VOCABULARY CANNOT LIVE IN bootstrap-contracts.ts. Task rail 7 and plan step 3 say to append new kinds to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, and bootstrap-contracts.ts is an owned path. Measured on disk, appending there breaks THREE files that are NOT owned by this task:
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:18 — `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` is `satisfies Readonly<Record<BootstrapCommandKind, ...>>`, a TOTAL record. A tenth kind with no entry is a typecheck failure in a foreign file.
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.test.ts:51 — `expect(BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS).toHaveLength(9)` plus set equality against a restated literal (deliberately restated so widening cannot pass silently; mem:decision-daemon-bootstrap-command-ingress).
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts:110-113 — same length and set-equality pair.
On top of that, task-671578e5 is editing that exact file RIGHT NOW for J1 (its `goal.close` fixture is already in the shared tree), which is the file collision the daemon flagged at claim time.
RESOLUTION, entirely inside owned paths: apps/daemon/src/review/ owns its own `REVIEW_COMMAND_KINDS`, typed `as const satisfies readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]` so a typo cannot compile, with its own bounded-decode ingress mirroring the house shape. This is a precedented pattern in this package, not a second idiom invented here: recovery/doctor-commands.ts already owns `DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS` and work/work-ingress.ts owns `parseWorkRequest`. bootstrap-contracts.ts will NOT be touched at all, so the flagged collision with task-671578e5 disappears.
Kinds, all four already members of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS: `review.submit` (record one round), `escalation.decide` (explicit escalation at the cap), `qualification.replan` (successor replan + delta approval), `integration.accept_output` (acceptance qu

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for durable review rounds — DoD 1. Create apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.test.ts before the module. Assert: a review round submitted through the daemon is recorded by calling @moe/review's recordReviewRound and committing ITS verdict through the store's expected-version decision seam; the round survives a store reopen, proving it is durable rather than in-memory; and replaying the identical command returns the SAME terminal decision while leaving exactly ONE durable row — assert the row count by reading the store back, because 'the second call did not throw' is precisely what a double write also looks like. Assert that a round the pure layer rejects surfaces @moe/review's own code from REVIEW_REASON_CODES verbatim, not a locally invented one, and name the refusing LAYER, since the daemon's shape gate and a review validator can both answer. Red, because the module does not exist.

Implement apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts to green. Follow the house shape exactly: bounded decode, exact-shape gate against a frozen key list with a pinned schemaVersion literal, call the pure helper, commit only on acceptance, return a frozen discriminated union. The module composes and never decides — every review rule already lives in @moe/review, so if you find yourself writing a condition that decides a review outcome, that rule belongs upstream and the answer is report_blocked, not a local copy. Import @moe/review from its package ROOT specifier only; its exports map is exclusive and a deep subpath will not resolve at runtime, which is a wall this repo has hit repeatedly. Read every limit and vocabulary from the package's exported constants rather than copying values, since a local copy drifts while both sides stay internally consistent. Append any new kinds to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS rather than reordering it. Give the module its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — apps/daemon is now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate. Target under 250 lines.

Finding lineage, append-only — DoD 2, and the requirement most easily lost. Implement lineage persistence so a successor round APPENDS rather than updating: the natural implementation of 'record round 2' is to update the review record, and that would silently violate design 1101's requirement that old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain readable. Assert it the strong way: capture round 1's stored bytes, create round 2, then assert round 1 is still retrievable AND byte-identical — not merely that a new row appeared, which an update-in-place would also satisfy for the new row. Use findingFingerprint for finding identity rather than comparing prose, and test BOTH directions so the rule cannot collapse into string equality: two findings with different wording but the same typed subject and rule ARE the same finding; two with identical wording but different subjects are NOT. Assert every finding links evidence to a required change, and that a finding with no evidence link is refused with the pure layer's code.

Delta approval: invalidation and carry-forward — DoD 3. Implement the classification that shows changed hashes and sorts every affected node into exactly one of INVALIDATED or CARRY_FORWARD, driven by the pure layer's comparison rather than a local hash check. THE PROPERTY IS TOTALITY: every affected node lands in exactly one bucket, with no third silent outcome and no node left unclassified — an unclassified node is the defect this DoD exists to catch, because it would silently carry forward work whose inputs changed. Assert the classification set by SET EQUALITY against a hand-written list, and assert the case count is non-zero so a classifier that returns nothing cannot pass. Include the adversarial pair: a node whose hash is unchanged must carry forward, and the same node with one byte changed must invalidate — if both produce the same classification, the hash is not actually covering the content it claims to.

Round counter, escalation, and the acceptance gate — DoD 4 and DoD 6. Persist the round counter durably and enforce escalation, reading the limit from @moe/review's REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT rather than a local constant, since a copied limit drifts while both sides stay internally consistent. Test AT the boundary rather than near it: two unsuccessful rounds do NOT escalate, the third REQUIRES explicit escalation, and a fourth cannot quietly proceed as if unescalated. Then the acceptance gate, which is the security-shaped half: a reviewer who fails assessReviewerIndependence, or a finding whose proof state is failed or UNKNOWN, cannot produce an acceptance — and the attempt must commit NOTHING, proven by reading the store back rather than by the returned value, since a handler that mutates and then refuses passes a return-value-only assertion. Treat failed and UNKNOWN as SEPARATE fixtures: 'we checked and it failed' and 'we could not tell' are different facts and only one of them might later become provable.

Prove the guards are load-bearing, then run the gates. MUTATION DRILL at each mechanism's single source: the append-only lineage guard, the findingFingerprint comparison, the invalidate-versus-carry-forward hash check, the escalation limit read, and the independence gate. Neutralise each operand with a constant — NEVER delete a line, since a deleted line from a multi-line condition is a syntax error that reddens the suite for the wrong reason and proves nothing. Count failed SUITES as well as failed tests and confirm the red test is the one naming that guard's code. Two mutations matter most: replacing the fingerprint comparison with text equality must redden the repeat-detection test, and removing the append-only guard must redden the byte-identity assertion — if either survives, that DoD is untested however green the suite looks. This worktree is shared and another agent's completion hook can commit your mutation, so capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` before each drill and verify the restore against that sha rather than `git status`. Then run fresh: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck, all exiting 0, and confirm every new module has its .js bridge.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec, and state what remains. Review: can any earlier round's findings be rewritten, dropped or reclassified by a later round, through ANY route; can a finding evade repeat detection by rewording; can a node come out of delta approval unclassified, or classified the same way whether or not its hash changed; can an acceptance be produced by a non-independent reviewer or on failed/UNKNOWN proof; is any review rule restated in the daemon instead of consumed from @moe/review; is the round limit read from the package or copied; does any refusal surface a locally invented code where the pure layer's should have survived; is @moe/review imported anywhere by a deep subpath. Then stage and commit by EXPLICIT PER-FILE pathspec — never a bare git commit, never git add -A, and NEVER a directory pathspec under apps/daemon/src/, since sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ in the same tree. Run `git status --porcelain` first and unstage foreign paths. Finally record in the completion evidence that this closes J4's persistence only: the Foundation canary also needs J1's command path (task-671578e5) and J3's launcher/restart composition, which is still unowned. A green J4 must not be read as a green canary.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) COMPOSITION ONLY, and the file layout enforces it. @moe/review already publishes 23 pure symbols covering every J4 rule; this task writes decode + persist + report and nothing else. Each daemon module here should read as 'parse, call the pure helper, commit its verdict' — if a module starts containing an `if` that decides a review outcome, that rule belongs in @moe/review and the answer is report_blocked, not a local copy.
(2) THE IMMUTABILITY HALF IS THE ONE THAT WILL BE MISSED. Design 1101's final clause — old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan — is easy to satisfy accidentally and easy to break accidentally, because the natural implementation of 'record round 2' is to update the review record. It must APPEND a successor and leave round 1 byte-identical. I gave it its own step and its own byte-comparison assertion rather than folding it into the lineage step.
(3) INVALIDATED vs CARRY_FORWARD IS A TOTAL CLASSIFICATION. Every affected node must land in exactly one bucket; a third silent outcome or an unclassified node is the defect. Asserted by set equality plus a non-zero case count, because a classifier that returns nothing would otherwise pass.
(4) ROUND LIMIT READ FROM THE PACKAGE, NEVER COPIED. @moe/review exports REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT. A local `const MAX_ROUNDS = 3` would drift the day the pure layer changes and the drift would be invisible — both sides would still be internally consistent.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
VERIFIED ON DISK 2026-08-09.
**@moe/review root exports (23, all pure, all reachable from the package root):** EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE, REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS, REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS, REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES, REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_LEVEL, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, REVIEW_LEASE_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_FORBIDDEN_ITEM_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_VERSION, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, assessReviewerIndependence, buildReviewPackage, findingFingerprint, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, recordReviewRound, reviewerCalibrationDigest.
**`apps/daemon/src` has NO review/ directory** — contents are bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery, work, index.ts. This task creates review/.
**The handler shape to copy** is stated in `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:48`: 'One shape for every project command: reduce, then commit only on acceptance.' Concretely: bounded decode, exact-shape gate against a frozen key list with a pinned schemaVersion literal, call the pure layer, commit through the store, return a frozen discriminated union.
**Durability seam:** @moe/store's `commitExpectedVersionDecision` yields one durable terminal decision and returns disposition REPLAYED on replay — that is what DoD 1's idempotence rides on. `readCommandDecisionsAfter` is the read-back path for proving non-mutation.
**Command vocabulary:** `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS` in bootstrap-contracts.ts:26 currently holds nine kinds; append, never reorder — existing suites assert against it.
**Bridges:** apps/daemon has .js bridges now (27 non-test .ts / 19 .js) and loads under plain Node; a new module without its sibling bridge will fail the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate that now exists.
**Design authority:** line 1101 of the pinned design defines J4. Read it directly (read-only — epic rail 1) rather than trusting the task description's paraphrase.
**findingFingerprint is the identity function for repeat detection** — use it rather than comparing prose, since two findings differing only in wording but sharing a typed subject and rule ARE the same finding.
planningNotes.risks:
1. **The append-only property is the one most likely to be broken by a natural implementation.** 'Record round 2' reads like an update to a review record. It must append a successor and leave round 1 byte-identical. Assert by comparing the earlier round's stored bytes before and after the successor exists — not merely that a new row appeared.
2. **A locally copied round limit or reason code will drift invisibly.** Both sides stay internally consistent while disagreeing with each other. Read REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT and REVIEW_REASON_CODES from the package.
3. **Repeat-finding detection must use findingFingerprint, not text equality.** Two findings with different wording and the same typed subject are the same finding; two with identical wording and different subjects are not. Test BOTH directions or the rule collapses into string comparison.
4. **Deep imports of @moe/review will not resolve at runtime.** Its exports map is exclusive; this repo has lost several task-days to that exact wall across scheduler, runner and daemon. Import from the root specifier only.
5. **Prove non-mutation by reading the store back.** A handler that mutates then refuses passes a return-value-only assertion — this has been a recurring near-miss on this board.
6. **The escalation boundary is a count, so test AT it**: 2 does not escalate, 3 requires explicit escalation, 4 cannot proceed as if unescalated. 'Several rounds' is not a test.
7. **Do not extend @moe/review.** If a rule appears missing, that is a finding; adding it in the daemon puts a review rule where no review reviewer will look for it.
8. Commit hazard: sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ in the same tree. Never use a directory pathspec under apps/daemon/src/.
